Color becomes sound.

Chromaflow is an ambient instrument and a living fluid canvas. Droplets add dye and momentum to an incompressible fluid simulation. When they land, their horizontal position selects a note from the current chord. Each color plays a different sampled instrument. Choose a palette swatch to keep new droplets in that one color and voice, including automatic rain and blooms. Enable Cycle colors beside the palette to restore variety.

Sound is powered by WebAudioFont by Sergey Surikov, with 20 instruments from the FluidR3 GM soundfont by Frank Wen. All instrument samples and the playback engine are served with this site. The 12 added voices use a gentle attack envelope and an extended release for softer, overlapping swells. Reverb uses a locally generated stereo impulse response; delay uses a filtered feedback loop synchronized to the tempo.

The fluid uses semi-Lagrangian advection, pressure projection, and vorticity confinement. Your settings stay in this browser. No account or server-side storage is needed for the instrument.

A rhythm beneath the color

The optional Rhythm tab adds four percussion voices and a sixteen-step beat studio. Start with a groove, edit hits and accents, or generate evenly spaced patterns and rotate them into new rhythms. Ten percussion sounds are synthesized locally with Web Audio, with swing, humanize, and independent levels. Their timed hits create visible ripples, add momentum to the existing fluid, or both. No new dye or melodic notes are added by percussion.
